title: Indefinite leave to remain if you have a Skilled Worker, Health and Care Worker, T2 or Tier 2 visa: Salary requirements - GOV.UK

content.p: You need to be paid at least a minimum salary if you hold a T2, Skilled Worker or Health and Care Worker visa. How much you must be paid depends on your visa.
You’ll usually need to be paid at least whichever is the higher out of the following:

content.li: £41,700 per year
the ‘standard going rate’ for the type of work you’ll be doing

content.p: Example
Your salary is £42,000 per year, but the standard going rate for the job you’ll be doing is £45,000. You do not meet the usual salary requirements for this visa.
Each occupation code has its own annual going rate. Check the going rate for your job in the going rates table .

content.h2: When the salary requirements are different

content.p: The salary requirements are different if:

content.li: you work in healthcare or education
your job is on the Immigration Salary List
you got a certificate of sponsorship for your first Skilled Worker (or equivalent) visa before 4 April 2024 and have held Skilled Worker visas since then
you have an International Sportsperson, T2 Sportsperson or Tier 2 (Sportsperson) visa
you have a T2 Minister of Religion or Tier 2 (Minister of Religion) visa

content.h2: If you work in healthcare or education

content.p: There are different salary rules if you work in some healthcare or education jobs , where the going rate is based on national pay scales. You must be paid whichever is higher out of the following:

content.li: £25,000 per year
the ‘going rate’ based on national pay scales for the type of work you’ll be doing

content.p: Check your going rate in the table of national pay scales for either:

content.li: eligible healthcare jobs - listed by NHS pay band and area of the UK
eligible teaching and education leadership jobs - listed by role and area of the UK

content.p: Ask your employer if you’re not sure what your role or pay band is. These going rates apply whether you’re working in the public or private sector.

content.h3: If your job in healthcare has different salary requirements

content.p: If you’re on a Health and Care Worker visa and your job is in one of the occupation codes with different salary requirements , you must be paid whichever is higher out of the following:

content.li: £31,300 per year
£25,000 per year if your job is on the Immigration Salary List (or it was at the time you applied)
the ‘lower going rate’ for the type of work you’ll be doing

content.h2: If your job is on the Immigration Salary List

content.p: If you do not meet the usual salary requirements, and you do not work in healthcare or education, you might still be eligible.
If you’re on a Skilled Worker visa and your job is on the Immigration Salary List (or it was at the time you applied), you must be paid at least either:

content.li: £33,400 per year
the ‘standard going rate’ for the type of work you’ll be doing

content.p: Check the going rate for your job in the going rates table .

content.h2: If you got a certificate of sponsorship for your first Skilled Worker (or equivalent) visa before 4 April 2024

content.p: If you have continually held one or more Skilled Worker visas since then, you must be paid whichever is higher out of the following:

content.li: £31,300 per year
£25,000 per year if your job is on the Immigration Salary List, (or it was at the time you applied)
the ‘lower going rate’ for the type of work you’ll be doing

content.p: There are also different salary requirements if you were sponsored for a Tier 2 (General) visa in one of the following occupation codes:

content.li: 2111 Chemical scientists
2112 Biological scientists and biochemists
2113 Physical scientists
2114 Social and humanities scientists
2119 Natural and social science professionals not elsewhere classified
2150 Research and development managers
2311 Higher education teaching professionals

content.p: In this case, you must be paid whichever is higher out of the following:

content.li: £25,000 per year
the different going rate for the type of work you’ll be doing

content.p: Check the going rate for your job in the going rates table .

content.h2: If you have an International Sportsperson, T2 Sportsperson or Tier 2 (Sportsperson) visa

content.p: You must be paid £35,800 or more a year.
When working out your salary, you can only count earnings:

content.li: from your main job that you’re sponsored for
for up to 48 hours a week, if you’re paid hourly

content.h2: If you have a T2 Minister of Religion or Tier 2 (Minister of Religion) visa

content.p: You must be paid at least the same as UK workers in the same role, and meet national minimum wage requirements.
